headline: Google to publish Android developers addresses
pages: Google will require many Android app developers to share a phone number and address publicly starting next year. The change is meant to comply with the EU Digital Services Act, but Google says the contact details will be public worldwide. Developers have until February 1, 2027, to declare whether they are a trader under UK and European law. The definition broadly applies to anyone earning revenue from apps, especially regular or high revenue. Hobby and non-commercial developers are exempt. Self-declared traders will have their details shown from March 1. Google does not accept PO boxes, so independent developers may have to show a home address or pay for a registered agent.
Apple faces the same rules but will show addresses only in relevant European countries and accepts PO boxes with proof. Source: The Verge.
